title: Jude quotes the Book of Enoch

tellings.quote: Jude takes verbatim from the book of Enoch.

And behold! He cometh with ten thousands of ⌜His⌝ holy ones To execute judgement upon all, And to destroy ⌜all⌝ the ungodly: And to convict all flesh Of all the works ⌜of their ungodliness⌝ which they have ungodly committed, ⌜And of all the hard things which⌝ ungodly sinners ⌜have spoken⌝ against Him.

plain: The story is that the Letter of Jude, a short book of the New Testament, quotes the Book of Enoch, an ancient Jewish text left out of most Bibles. A filmmaker named Tim Alberino says so on the show, as a researcher stating it without a source: "Jude takes verbatim from the book of Enoch." Set beside his claim is the opening of Enoch itself, in the translation by R. H. Charles published in 1917. At chapter 1, verse 9, it says: "And behold! He cometh with ten thousands of His holy ones To execute judgement upon all, And to destroy all the ungodly." It goes on to say he will "convict all flesh" of their ungodly deeds and of the "hard things" sinners have spoken against him. That passage shows what Alberino means Jude repeats: a Lord coming with a vast host of holy ones to judge the ungodly. The tellings do not give Jude's own wording, so how close the two are word for word is left to the reader to check. If Alberino is right, an early Christian writer treated Enoch as scripture worth quoting, and that matters to people who read Enoch's stories of fallen angels and giants as history.
